raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through as Old Wang — 68 years old, farmed this same 8 mu for fifty years. My boy works in the city now, so it's just me and the wife. Here's how I'm planning this year.

---

**Wheat first** — that's the main one, goes in October after the maize comes off. I do about 4 mu of wheat and 4 mu of maize, same as always. No point changing a system that's fed us this long.

For fertilizer, I buy one bag of compound (那个复合肥) before planting — about 50 jin per mu as base. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, around jointing (起身拔节), I topdress urea, maybe 20-25 jin per mu. My neighbor Old Li tried cutting back last year and his yield dropped, so I'm not cutting. At my age, I can't afford a bad year — the pension isn't much.

I'll irrigate three times on wheat: once before winter (冬灌) so it doesn't freeze out, once at green-up, once at grain-filling if it's dry. The well costs money to run but wheat without water on this plain, forget it. I use the seed I bought two years ago from the seed station — 济麦22 I think it's called, works fine here.

**Maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in June, very tight, maybe 3-4 days to get it planted. I hire the neighbor's son with the planter now — my knees can't handle planting by hand anymore. Costs me 30 yuan per mu but worth it. For fertilizer I put one bag of compound at planting and topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (大喇叭口). Less than wheat, maize doesn't need as much on our soil. One irrigation usually, maybe two if July is dry.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once on both crops, that's standard. Insecticide only if I see the bugs. I don't spray for the sake of spraying, costs add up.

I don't hire much labor — me and the wife do most of it. Harvest I pay the combine operator, everybody does now. Can't swing a scythe at 68.
